scope_note: Third-pass public-evidence audit for NYSE Group's U.S. Liquidity Center at 1700 MacArthur Boulevard, Mahwah. The direct account retains operator-reported building area and total site electrical power, adds six historical assessor observations, the 2025 parcel tax bill, and verified 2024-2025 paid parcel charges. It separates the original 398,000-square-foot building from customer equipment, internal colocation-hall fit-outs, ICE's wider technology operations, and the landlord-led 142,250-square-foot Building 2. Direct investment, realized employment or payroll, supplier payments, community transfers, facility-only resource consumption, incentives, and public-service costs remain unavailable; bounded arithmetic and engineering sensitivities are kept in the separate modeled-synthesis fragment.

Area and power are facility capacity descriptors, not occupied area, IT load, utilization, annual electricity, tenant equipment ownership or economic contribution.

project_updates.title: Boundary, operator and chronology reconciled
project_updates.notes: NYSE/ICE technical specifications, operating policies, SEC filings, SRO notices, Township dockets 1456-19 and 1532-22, Russo's timeline and the IM3 building geometry were reviewed for 2007-2026 using NYSE Group, NYSE Euronext, Intercontinental Exchange, ICE Global Network, USLC, Mahwah Data Center, 1700 MacArthur, block 139 lot 4, Hall 5 and Hall 6. The selected account is the original 398,000-square-foot, two-story building; ICE operates the Mahwah Data Center through Fixed Income and Data Services, while NYSE markets, other ICE systems and customers use the facility. Internal colocation-hall fit-outs remain within the building, customer cabinets and equipment remain tenant scope, and ICE's regional/global access-center and data-center portfolio is excluded.
project_updates.project_description: NYSE Group's U.S. Liquidity Center is the original 398,000-square-foot, two-story office-and-data-center building at 1700 MacArthur Boulevard in Mahwah, Bergen County, operated by Intercontinental Exchange through its Fixed Income and Data Services business. NYSE signed the purpose-built lease in 2007, and the operator says the site has housed NYSE markets since 2010 and has 28 MW of total site electrical power. This building-level account includes later colocation-hall fit-outs within the original facility but excludes customers' equipment and the landlord-led 142,250-square-foot Building 2 proposed next to it.

project_updates.title: Assessor, tax-collector and payment audit
project_updates.notes: New Jersey MOD-IV archives, Rutgers' MOD-IV historical database, Mahwah WIPP account 5447, the Township Tax Collector page, school-district ACFR principal-taxpayer tables, zoning ownership records and a secondary parcel-history index were searched by district 0233, block 139 lot 4, account 5447, 1700 MacArthur, MacArthur Boulevard LLC, NYSE and ICE for tax years 2007-2026. Six historical assessed values, the complete 2025 bill and complete 2024-2025 paid charges are retained. Primary ACFR observations now cover 2011, 2012 and 2018-2021; the formerly indexed 2017 state URL now returns 404, and 2013-2017 remain corroborated only by a secondary index and are not promoted. The 2019 ACFR's retrospective 2010 row conflicts with parcel-history evidence and is excluded. The live account shows class 4A, $102 million total assessed value, zero exemption and no deductions; 2023 has $4,409.86 of adjustments and is not normalized as paid, while 2026 is partial-year. Parcel payments do not identify remitter or economic incidence and do not equal municipality-only receipts.

project_updates.title: Planning, permit and environmental audit separates Building 2
project_updates.notes: Mahwah Planning and Zoning Board records were searched for dockets 651, 651A, 1456-19 and 1532-22; Highlands monthly reports, NJ DCA Construction Reporter files and NJDEP/BPU web results were searched for 1700 MacArthur, block 139 lot 4, MacArthur Boulevard LLC, NYSE, ICE, data center, generators, cooling towers, soil movement, stormwater and towers across 2009-2026. Docket 651/651A and the Highlands record establish a landlord-led 142,250-square-foot Building 2 adjacent to the existing building; permit 20251408 reports $13.5 million at the shared address but no operator or tenant. The amount is excluded because the address alone cannot attribute later-building cost to NYSE/ICE or the selected building. Docket 1532-22's denied towers likewise do not establish realized expansion spending.

project_updates.title: Incentive, compliance and public-finance audit
project_updates.notes: NJEDA completed/certified incentive projects and public award materials, New Jersey Treasury property-tax access, Bergen County abstracts of ratables, Mahwah 2024 Annual Financial Statement, adopted budgets and meeting records were searched for NYSE, NYSE Group, ICE, Intercontinental Exchange, MacArthur Boulevard LLC, 1700 MacArthur, grant, incentive, tax credit, PILOT, abatement, bond, reimbursement and infrastructure for 2007-2026. No project-linked NJEDA award, certified credit, municipal grant, bond proceeds, tax abatement, PILOT, TIF, waived fee, reimbursement, check-register disbursement or project-level public cost was found. The certified 2025 rate components reconcile exactly to the parcel bill and support modeled school, municipal and county allocations; they do not disclose recipient cash timing or marginal cost. The NJEDA list's Mahwah entry is Ascena/Dress Barn, not this site. Program-specific absence does not prove zero subsidy or zero public cost.

project_updates.title: Utility and resource audit preserves meter and scope limits
project_updates.notes: Mahwah WIPP utility accounts 203167-0 and 203167-1, Township water/sewer rate sheets, ICE technical specifications and operating policies, and exact searches of BPU, NJDEP, Rockland Electric, Orange & Rockland, JCP&L, PSE&G and PJM sources were reviewed using 1700 MacArthur, block 139 lot 4, NYSE, ICE, water, sewer, electricity, demand, tariff, interconnection, generator, fuel, emissions and discharge. The live account provides four consecutive quarterly water usage values and paid charges, while the Township rate sheet establishes that Mahwah bills actual water usage in cubic feet. A modeled unit conversion is retained for the rolling four-quarter parcel account, not as calendar-year consumption or an original-building allocation. The 28 MW specification remains capacity, not observed demand or annual use; a wide utilization sensitivity is retained separately. No facility electricity bill, tariff determinant, generator runtime, fuel use, emissions or utility contribution is normalized.

project_updates.title: Workforce, payroll and training audit
project_updates.notes: ICE careers and support pages, the Mahwah operating policies, SEC annual filings, New Jersey labor/workforce access, Bergen County QCEW/OEWS/CBP materials and exact web searches were checked for Mahwah, USLC, data center operations, employees, FTE, jobs, payroll, wages, benefits, occupations, worker residence, construction labor, apprenticeship and training from 2007-2026. A current Senior Engineer vacancy confirms a Mahwah data-center occupation but not a filled job. The facility policies say the Data Center Operations team supporting Mahwah incidents is available 24x7; a zero-leave one-post coverage equivalent is retained with employment location and employer relationship unallocated because the document does not say the team is onsite. No site headcount, annual-average FTE, compensation, local-resident share, apprenticeship enrollment, training completion, construction job-years or local hire count was found. County industry averages are not assigned to the facility.

project_updates.title: Supplier and procurement audit identifies roles, not payments
project_updates.notes: NYSE/ICE filings and policies, Russo records, ENR archives, Mahwah planning exhibits and direct searches used Structure Tone, Russo Development, MacArthur Boulevard LLC, Corgan, Lapatka Associates, Ahead Engineering, Anova Financial Networks, contractor, vendor, supplier, subcontractor, procurement, invoice and payment for 2007-2026. Russo is documented as developer/landlord, Structure Tone as original interior-build-out manager, Corgan and Lapatka as Building 2 professionals, and Anova in telecommunications/connectivity records. No source supplies a selected-building contract value, paid amount, subcontractor roster, vendor production location, Bergen County purchase share or locally retained supplier spend. Customer shipments and hardware are not operator procurement.

project_updates.title: Community and recipient-side audit
project_updates.notes: ICE/NYSE newsroom, sustainability and grant materials, Mahwah budgets/minutes, school and local nonprofit results, and recipient-side web searches were reviewed for Mahwah, Bergen County, NYSE, ICE, USLC, donation, grant, sponsorship, school, nonprofit, volunteer and first responder from 2007-2026. ICE's 2020 $10 million COVID program was global across 35 office cities and does not name Mahwah, the facility or a Bergen County allocation. No recipient accounting, payment date, restriction, in-kind valuation or volunteer-hour amount tied to the USLC was found. Regional or corporate philanthropy is not assigned to this building and the unresolved amount is not coded as zero.

project_updates.title: Filings, archives and local-reporting gap closure
project_updates.notes: SEC EDGAR properties disclosures and exchange rule filings, Federal Register notices, ICE/NYSE document archives, Mahwah Agenda Center records, NJ Highlands/DCA sources and local/trade reporting were searched for 2007-2026. The record establishes the 2007 lease, 2010 operations, Hall 5 opening after the 2024 customer ordering window and Hall 6 development in 2025. Customer power deposits are invoice credits and do not establish ICE investment; internal hall expansions do not change the 398,000-square-foot building boundary. No audited facility revenue, operating expense, rack occupancy, capital outlay, rent, customer-equipment value or local economic contribution was disclosed.

project_updates.title: Model candidate rejected — facility investment
project_updates.notes: Candidate: multiply 398,000 square feet by an industry construction-cost-per-square-foot coefficient, or treat assessed value as investment. Rejected: the only per-square-foot amount found is a 2010 industry-wide trade estimate rather than a project contract, while assessed value is a taxable stock and the same parcel now includes later planning. No project-specific land price, base-building cost, fit-out cost, equipment spend, lease capitalization or expenditure timing exists; transferred cost coefficients would create false precision.

project_updates.title: Model candidate rejected — construction jobs, payroll and local spend
project_updates.notes: Candidate: apply job-year, labor-income or local-purchase coefficients to permit 20251408 or an inferred original construction cost. Rejected: the $13.5 million permit is at the shared address and planning evidence links later construction to landlord-led Building 2, outside the selected original building; no original project expenditure base, work schedule, worker hours, payroll, contractor payments, supplier geography or local-retention share is public. The model would compound a boundary error with transferred coefficients.

project_updates.title: Model candidates accepted — electricity sensitivity and rolling water withdrawal
project_updates.notes: Candidate A: annualize 28 MW of operator-reported total site electrical power at 25%, 50% and 100% average utilization. Accepted only as a wide facility-electricity sensitivity and theoretical ceiling; no PUE is applied because 28 MW is already total-site power, and no scenario is actual demand, consumption, tenant allocation, cost or emissions. Candidate B: sum four consecutive WIPP water-usage fields and convert the Township's cubic-foot billing unit to gallons. Accepted as a rolling four-quarter parcel-account withdrawal, not calendar-year consumption or a selected-building allocation. Electricity cost, emissions, cooling water and wastewater remain rejected because tariff determinants, meter boundaries, PUE/WUE and discharge are unresolved.

project_updates.title: Model candidates accepted — recipient allocations and public-cost break-even
project_updates.notes: Candidate A: apply the certified 2025 school, municipal and county rate components to the same parcel's $102 million assessment. Accepted because the six published components sum to the 2.127 general rate and reconcile exactly to the parcel's $2,169,540 billed and paid total; the allocations remain modeled, recipient-level levy incidence rather than cash receipts. Candidate B: state the same-account marginal public-service and incentive-cost break-even threshold at $2,169,540. Accepted as a decision threshold, not an estimate of cost or net benefit: positive fiscal margin would require all same-recipient 2025 marginal costs and incentives to be below the threshold, and negative margin would require them to exceed it. Actual costs remain unobserved.

project_updates.title: Model candidate accepted — 24x7 support coverage; broader workforce models rejected
project_updates.notes: Candidate A: translate the Mahwah operating policy's role-specific statement that the Data Center Operations team is available 24x7 into the zero-leave FTE-equivalent needed to cover one simultaneous support post. Accepted as a conditional 8,760/2,080 mathematical floor with the work location, employer/contractor relationship and onsite status explicitly unallocated. Candidate B: infer facility jobs or payroll from that floor, vacancies, floor area or 28 MW and apply Bergen County wages or multipliers. Rejected because actual posts, headcount, schedules, location, residence, compensation and payroll are not reported; supplier and household effects would inherit those unsupported inputs.

project_updates.title: Model candidate rejected — community contribution
project_updates.notes: Candidate: allocate ICE's global philanthropy to Mahwah by office count, building area, employees or equal shares, or encode no located recipient payment as zero. Rejected: the global program provides no facility allocation, Mahwah recipient, employee denominator or restriction linking funds to the USLC. Corporate portfolio philanthropy cannot be apportioned to this building, and absence of public recipient evidence is an unresolved gap rather than a zero-valued contribution.

project_updates.title: Model candidate rejected — county outcome attribution
project_updates.notes: Candidate: calculate before-after or comparison-county changes in Bergen County employment, wages or GDP around 2010 and label the gap a NYSE contribution. Rejected: the facility's opening is a single event within a large, diversified county, NYSE moved and consolidated technology functions across locations, other data centers and macroeconomic changes overlap, and no comparison county, parallel-trend evidence, treatment share or worker-residence bridge was established. County outcome series remain context, not attributable impact.
